2B armour.summary:
Package 2B (armour and damage, spec §6) is built and committed on branch ground/armour, on top of 6672523. It touches js/armour.js (the Armour region only; SHELLS is unchanged), the bodies of damage and explode in js/combat.js, sendHits and onHit in js/mp.js, test/armour.test.js (77 checks) and 3 checks in test/ground.test.js. The headless suite passes with every old baseline identical.

**Hit geometry**
- `hitAll` finds every part a segment crosses, sorted by entry, each with its entry and exit faces.
  - Prisms are clipped with Cyrus–Beck against the outline's edges and the two sides. Parts with no outline are clipped as a box.
  - Round parts are upright cylinders with caps. The wall normal is tilted by `round.slope`, and each hit keeps the cosine of its bearing.
  - Old parts on a plated vessel are hit by their old `boxesOf` boxes.
  - Turned turrets (nested rings too) and raised or swung barrels are handled: the segment is turned into each part's own frame about its trunnion.
- `hitFirst` answers the way `hitVessel` does.
- Speed: each part shape is cached per def, each vessel's parts as records (`v._arm`). Parts are culled by bounding spheres before any transform, and turn sines and cosines are cached.

**What a shell does (`resolve`, then `apply`)**
- Plates: thickness by face (`p.mm`, edge, sides, bearing, roof; open faces count 0), normalisation, overmatch at ×0.6 with no ricochet, `min(t/cos, 6t)`, and composite's strength against HEAT.
- Ricochets use seeded smoothstep windows. A kinetic one leaves as a new shell at 0.6 of its speed and half its penetration, and never bounces again.
- Screens:
  - Skirts make HEAT go off early (×0.7, minus 250 mm a metre of air gap).
  - Slat cages crush about half of non-tandem HEAT.
  - Reactive bricks take −100 mm off kinetic rounds and −400 off HEAT, and are blown off (a tandem charge ignores the first one).
  - Applique plates subtract their effective thickness.
- Penetration needs `pen ≥ eff`. Between 0.8 and 1 of `eff`, a non-penetration has a 30% chance of 2 fragments inside.
- HESH ignores the plate's angle up to 60° and beats plates up to 120 mm. HE bursts through `explode`.
- Parts with no armour take the shell's whole damage. A kinetic round goes on with 10 mm less, and an unplated craft is passed through (`s.skip`). So SPAA rounds still kill planes.
- After penetration (deterministic, seeded from the shot serial and the vessel):
  - The path damages each part it crosses by `dmg·(1 − 0.5·s/L)`. An engine takes 30 mm out of what is left, ammunition 10. A far face the remainder can't beat stops it.
  - Fragments: `n·clamp(res/40 + 0.5)` rays in the cone; the first thing each meets takes 45 ± 15, so a fuel cell stops them.
  - The APHE burst hits modules within its radius, shielded by fuel cells.
  - The plate takes 10% of the shell's damage on a penetration, 3% otherwise.

**Modules, crew and knock-out**
- `moduleDown` breaks a part and leaves it in place; calling it again does nothing.
- `modDamage` keeps hp in `host.mods`; it respects spawn protection and inactive modules.
- `crewOf` applies the rule that placed seats and racks replace a host's built-in crew and ammunition. `has` is true for old craft and craft with an old cab, and false once knocked out.
- Role swaps after 4 s, in the order loader, radio operator, commander.
- Knock-out happens below `min(2, crew)` alive, on a detonation, or when a ground vehicle's hull or turret reaches 0 hp. It sets `p.ko`, calls `sim.onDestroyed` and `aiDown`, and the hulk stays.
- A detonation blasts everything nearby except the hulk, then throws the turret (+9 m/s up, 1–3 rad/s tumble, twice that in Hollywood).
- Cook-off odds follow the formula, +0.2 against HEAT, APHE and HE; a blow-out bustle vents instead.
- Fires: engines by fuel type, fuel cells and built-in fuel. `repairStep` runs fires, swaps and repairs (stopped, 6 s unhurt, with a crew, worst first).
- `partFX`, module toasts, `Armour.fb`, haptics and `summary` are done.

**Shells in flight (`moveShell`)**
- Each shell has its own drag. It tests vessels (skipping its owner for 1.5 s), range targets and the HE-VT proximity fuze.
- The ground is skipped above `gTop` and tested every 2nd step. Within 6 m of the ground the segment is sampled every 5 m and a hit is bisected. Cheap rounds use the 16 m `coarseH` cache. The ground in front of a vessel is checked before the vessel is hit.
- `netShell` builds a damage-free copy with the ghost gun's flash, `shotAt` and `Sound.cannon`.

**HE and old weapons**
- The plated branch of `explode` measures turned-turret distances and calls `blastK` (overmatch of the thinnest face toward the blast, inner parts through their host, the 20 mm rule for gear, guns and radars).
- `legacyHit` uses the spec's table for old bullets, rockets, missiles and bombs.

**Multiplayer**
- `sendHits` gains module rows (at most 32), `d` and `h`. It still sends when only module rows hit, and refuses wrecks. Old messages are byte-identical.
- `onHit` checks every module row: id, whole index in range, finite damage clamped to 2000. It uses `d` if it is sane, else the shooter's bearing.

**Measured (Node):** a penetration with everything after it costs 70 µs mean (budget 100). A main-gun shell over its life costs 0.29 ms (budget 3), an autocannon round 0.14 ms (budget 0.3).
deviations: Tracks and armoured wheels act as spaced plates in front of the hull. If the round beats one, the track takes 50% of the shell's damage and the rest goes on into the hull; otherwise 15% (30% for HEAT) and the round stops. Treating them as 'the first structural part' with post-penetration from the track would skip the hull's side plate.
Guns have no def.armour, so they follow the critic's rule for unarmoured parts (whole damage, a kinetic round goes on with 10 mm less), not the 'structural' row.

HEAT jets lose 250 mm a metre over every air gap after they go off, measured from the far side of each part crossed; skirts also apply ×0.7. So going off on reactive bricks, applique plates or tracks costs only the real gap.
HEAT, HESH and HE rounds that ricochet fly on as dud shells (no burst, no damage); kinetic ricochets follow the spec.

A direct HE hit always bursts through explode (blastK decides). It reports 'pen' when its he value is at least the struck face's thickness. HESH also bursts outside (its blast, at 0.3 of its damage), on top of its 12 fragments.

The path also damages gun breeches and turret rings (modules inside) as well as inner parts and module spheres. The far-face check uses the exit face's effective thickness. Placed fuel cells shield modules from the APHE burst.

Ground-vehicle control parts (hulls, turrets) at 0 hp go to Armour.moduleDown, which knocks the vehicle out and leaves the hulk, instead of destroyPart breaking it apart (in combat.js damage). The detonation's explode spares the hulk itself.

The hit message gains an optional h: 1 for 'hot' rounds (HEAT, APHE, HE), so the victim can add +0.2 to cook-off odds. Signatures gain optional trailing arguments: sendHits(…, hot), modDamage(…, hot), blastK(…, at), apply(v, res, F, by, s). Armour.hot is a module flag.
coarseH(a, z, b) takes the body angle and depth, as Terrain.surfaceAt does, not (e, z). It returns the highest of the 4 lattice corners (conservative) rather than an interpolated height.

Seat swaps happen only for seats emptied by a death, not for designs that never had a gunner. The spec's order (loader, radio, commander) means a dead driver is replaced by the loader first if he is alive.
has() is true for old craft and for any vessel with an old cab or cockpit, and false once knocked out.
summary.front is the weakest forward plate against a level shot: the TK-34's 53° lower plate, 75 mm, not its 99 mm glacis.
Repairs restore every module to 60% (the spec gives 60% only for the engine). A damaged store loses ceil(rounds·min(1, dmg/hp)·0.5) rounds.
Module toasts are silent after a knock-out. netShell drops shots faster than 3000 m/s, and drops all copies once Combat.S.shots holds more than 2000.
openIssues: render3d.js syncCombat has no pool for k 'shell' (CB.pool['shell'] is undefined) and throws, silently, every frame. 3F's shell route must land before shells reach the page: 2C's Aim.fire, netShell copies and ricochets.

For 2C:
- legacyHit reads s.pen (weapon.heat), s.tandem and s.he from ATGM and rocket shots, falling back to 120 or 700 mm.
- Shells without pen, v0 or life fall back to their SHELLS entry; s.n (a serial) is set lazily.
- Store rounds live on p.rounds (racks) and host.mrounds[i] (built-in), read and written through the getter/setter on crewOf(v).stores[].rounds.
- has() is false once knocked out.

For 3G: v.ko = { why: 'crew'|'ammo'|'hull', x (detonated), t } gives down's x; tossed turret pieces have q.tossed. Armour.fb.ko is set only for local knock-outs, so onDown must set it in rooms. MP.startFlight should set v.spawnAt.
For 3F: Armour.fb = { shot: { r, what, crew, t }, hurt: [{ d, t }], ko }; v.repair = { p, name, t, T, on } for 'Stop to repair' and 'Repairing'. The knock-out modal still says 'Vessel destroyed'.
For 2A: tracks, wheels and engines are p.broken; engine power uses Combat.hpFrac; Armour.has(v, 'driver') is false once knocked out.
Not saved in flights (vessel.js GV_SAVE): store rounds (p.rounds, p.mrounds), seat swaps (p.roles, p.role), fires, v.ko, v.vent, v.swaps. A restored flight has full stores and loses swaps.

Balance for 3I: an 85 mm APHE penetration often knocks out a TK-34 at once, because the 2 m burst reaches the turret crew through the hull roof. Full racks cook off at 0.9–0.95. This matches War Thunder's lethality but may want tuning.
The bench and docs are not mine: test/bench/ground-bench.mjs (2A edits it), handbook §4, the test/README armour row and README are Phase 4's. sw.js stays at overbuilt-v24, which has not shipped yet.
outsideScope: test/ground.test.js (§contract): three checks pinned Phase 1's stand-ins and now pin the real behaviour. A module part at 0 hp breaks and stays. An old round on armour is resolved: up through the 22.5 mm belly, the hull takes 10%. 'Armour.hitFirst stands in…' was renamed to 'Armour.hitFirst: through a plain box…'.

2A movement.summary:
Package 2A (Movement) is done: all of spec §4 is in /home/user/Overbuilt/.claude/worktrees/wf_183678f7-15d-1/js/gear.js (squashed onto 6672523; branch ground/movement).

**Gear.ground (§4.2-4.6, 4.8)**
- **Probes and plane fit.** One surfaceAt per road wheel or armoured wheel, plus the spot under the centre of mass (deckAt, surfaceAt, waterAt). A least-squares plane through those heights gives one normal nG for every contact. If the fit fails (one track down, on its side or roof), it falls back to normalAt(L0).
- **Hull corners.** With gear down last step and a valid fit, a corner is probed only inside the 0.6 m + 0.02/m band over the plane. The test is a single dot product in part space. Probes are taken lowest first, capped so a step stays at 15 Gear calls plus the vessel's own groundHeight, 16 in all (the MA-1's skirts add 8 low corners). Without gear contact last step, corners use the old lim0 cull, so a rollover is still caught.
- **Cheaper parked steps.** Probe heights are kept while a probe has moved less than 2 mm (re-read every 120 steps). The spot is kept for 0.5 m (or 15 steps). Probe spots are linearised from the centre of mass instead of calling locate: worst error 18 µm.
- **Crash, dent, bouncy, contactTime, landed, restTime.** Copied line for line from vessel.js (side-of-deck and prop rules included). vessel.js has a comment naming the copy; nothing else in vessel.js changed.
- **Suspension.** k = m·g/(N·0.4·travel), c = 2ζ√(k·m/N), ζ 0.45 (0.08 with the 'bouncy' setting), applied once along nG. Past the travel, an accumulated rigid bump stop takes over.
- **Traction.** Four iterations of accumulated impulses: bump stops and hull normals, traction toward each side's belt speed, sideways grip, then hull friction as vessel.js does it. Traction is clamped to mu·JN. An impulse that adds energy is paid from the side's power budget, shared between contacts by load; braking is free. Coasting brakes at 0.18 g plus the slope. Iterations stop early once converged.
- **Steering.** Skid steering comes from the belt speeds, and the difference between the sides is held while the engine is power-limited, so the tank turns under full throttle. Armoured wheels steer like a car, roll as an open differential, and get a skid assist below 3 m/s. A broken track or wheel has mu 0.05 on its side. Rolling resistance is on (off in water).
- **Water.** Wading uses mu 0.12 and 2 m/s; amphibious hulls use 0.35 and 3.5 m/s. Flooding toasts "Engine flooded!" and "Engine restarted".
- **Righting.** 3·m·g·B, capped at 2 rad/s, until within 20°; it sets v.righting.
- **Outputs.** Physics writes p.belt, p.spin, v.beltV, v.susp, v.drivePower, v.flooded and v.righting, and keeps wheelsDown, canDrive, wheelSpeed and steer current. There is no per-step allocation.

**Gear.bump (§4.7)**
- A sphere test on body-box radii, then a 15-axis separating-axis test on body boxes (bodyBox, or bounds for old craft).
- Ghosts, kinematic AI and wrecks don't move. Another local vessel shares the push by mass and takes the opposite impulse; a woken sleeper has its restTime reset. Push-out is capped at 0.1 m a step, restitution 0.15, friction 0.3.
- Ramming above 6 m/s dents the nearest part's box through Combat.impact (local only).

**Gear.stats(parts)** is pure and returns { mass, kw, hpt, top, rev, pivot, climb, tip, overload, loadT } plus top0 and B. It returns null for a design with no ground-update parts.

- Parked meets ≤ 40 µs; driving does not meet ≤ 80 µs.
- Most of a driving step is terrain.js: each surfaceAt costs ~5 µs in the test vm. With flat stub terrain a driving step costs 32 µs.
- Collisions: 0.63 µs a call with 12 tanks 9 m apart, 4.1 µs packed 3.6 m apart side by side (budget 5 µs).

**Real page (Playwright, software WebGL, 1280×720 and 390×844):** the TK-34 and Pumo launched from the builder drive, turn and park, with no console errors. Screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Overbuilt/0587f056-6c41-58cd-9f76-3deee688a95a/scratchpad/ground/scratch-2a/ (drive-*.png).

**Test vehicles:** /home/user/Overbuilt/.claude/worktrees/wf_183678f7-15d-1/test/lib/tanks.js exports { tk34, ms4, tygr, ma1, pumo }, built from the exact §12 parts. They are joined, clash-free, priced exactly as §12, and within 1% of its masses.
deviations: The power budget uses each side's actual mean contact speed (floored at 1.5 m/s). Using the belt target speed would make 0–30 km/h take about 12 s.
Driving versus braking is decided by energy (dJ·(vt + dJ·et/2) > 0), not by the target's sign. Without this, braking against motion was billed as driving.
Budgets (drive and coast) are shared between contacts by load. A shared pool used up in list order put yaw into a coasting tank.

Rolling resistance scales with speed: crr·m·g·min(1, v/Vmax). The table's 0–30 times assume no rolling resistance at low speed; with a constant crr, the MS-4 and Tygr missed by 41% and 46%. It is off in water, so wading reaches 2 m/s.

Skid-steer lateral model: a track's sideways grip resists sliding and rolling but not the hull's yaw, up to 1.15 × turn × the power factor; past that it scrubs fully. With Coulomb lateral grip of 0.6 on 3 contacts per track, the MS-4 could not pivot and a broken track could not swing.
The belts' difference is held around the current mean speed while power-limited (outer side drives, inner side held back). Without it the tank would not turn while accelerating.
A/D alone at speed: the belts' mean follows the hull's speed (coasting), so the tank turns as it rolls to a stop instead of slamming the brakes and then pivoting.

Coasting brakes at (0.18 + the slope's sine)·m·g, so a tank rolling down a hill still slows and the parking brake catches it. The parking-brake threshold uses speed along the ground, so a landing bounce doesn't release it.
At rest only the velocity along the ground is zeroed; the springs carry the weight. Zeroing all of it sank the hull onto its bump stops.
When braking or parked, the step gravity moved the tank along the ground is undone, so it doesn't creep down slopes (it crept 2 cm/s on 15°).

Armoured wheels: open-differential targets (each wheel's own speed round the current turn). Steering is δ = min(0.5, 0.45·g·L/v²), with L the distance between the steered and unsteered axles. The spec's 5·wheelbase/v² with the 8×8's full wheelbase made the Pumo plough and stall.

Flooding: depth is the water surface minus the bed (one heightAt, only in water). The engine floods when depth > 1.4 m and above the lowest engine part. After 5 s flooded it runs at 20% power so the crew can crawl out of the solid sea (otherwise it is stuck for good). It restarts 5 s after leaving the water, toasting 'Engine restarted'. Toasts go only to the active vessel.
Righting: capped at 2 rad/s about its axis; once started it is not cancelled by speed over 3 m/s; after 6 s it gives up and tries again. No toast is shown: 3F displays v.righting.
Belly probes are capped (lowest first) so an upright step uses at most 15 Gear calls, 16 with physicsStep's own groundHeight.
For speed, probe heights are kept for 2 mm of movement (re-read every 120 steps), the spot for 0.5 m or 15 steps, and probe spots are linearised from the centre of mass.

gear.js uses script-scope aliases (gMath, gQrot, …) and const arrow helpers. In the vm the tests use, every page-global lookup goes through the sandbox; this halved the step's own cost. It makes no difference in a page.

Gear.stats: tip subtracts the springs' lean (2·sag/B); top uses the speed-scaled rolling resistance and leaves out air drag; it adds top0 and B. overload is the tonnes over the rating (0 when within it).

Collisions: when the other vessel is local, both are resolved in one bump. Push-out is capped at 0.1 m a step so split debris doesn't jump. The ram dent ratio is 0.75 + (v − 6)/(4 × breakSpeed), applied to the part whose box is nearest the contact.

2C aim.summary:
Package 2C (aim and weapons) is written in full with file tools but has never been run, so it is unverified and has no measured numbers. Before Bash was blocked I ran `node test/run.mjs` on the untouched base: all 19 suites passed with identical baselines (output in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Overbuilt/0587f056-6c41-58cd-9f76-3deee688a95a/scratchpad/ground/2c-base-run.txt). After that I could only read and edit files.

js/aim.js (the Phase 1 core is unchanged; every stub is now implemented):
- **Sweep and limits.** `Aim.sweep(parts, group)` is pure and cached by a layout signature. It returns `{ yawLim, dep, deps }`.
  - Traverse: in 5° steps, the turning members' footprints (boxes, or discs for round parts), turned about the ring, are tested against parts that don't turn and stand above the ring's top. yawLim is null for all the way round, and may run past ±180° one way.
  - Depression: each aimed part gets 12 sectors, tested at the sector's centre and ±15°. The barrel is a 10-point capsule (r 0.12 m) checked against the parts' outline prisms, discs and boxes; points that already sit inside something at the build pose are ignored. Over a raised deck the limit can be positive (the gun must lift).
  - `Aim.limits(v)` is computed lazily and again when `v.tg` changes.
- **Aim step, every physics substep.** It runs for the player when `F.groundAim` and `F.aim.P` are set, and for local ground AI at `v.aimP`. Order:
  1. Stabilisers first re-express last step's world direction in the new hull frame (ring stab 2, gun stab ≥1).
  2. Rings slew outer first. The wanted yaw corrects for how far the main weapon's trunnion sits off the ring's centre. Rates follow the cap formula, halved below 50% hp, 2°/s broken, 0 jammed. Yaw limits are respected.
  3. Each aimed part takes its own elevation and arc (trav, the casemate arc when in no group, else 0), clamped by el limits and the sector's depression.
     - Guns are lifted in the vertical plane: Arcade for the measured range, Realistic for `F.zero`.
     - AA guns aim at the intercept point while the tracking radar holds a lock.
     - Rocket rails are elevated from their range table; a tracking dish looks at its target.
  4. World directions are stored for the next step.
  - Unstabilised axes catch up only at their own rate.
  - `p._err` and `p._lim` are kept for the HUD.
  - No allocation per substep.
- **Firing.** Shells are fired along the actual barrel, with dispersion `disp × (stab ? 1+v/20 : 1+v/6)`, using the §6.1 shell object; `gTop` is the arena's measured top + 5 m, else ∞.
  - Main gun: one round per trigger edge. The ready rack (`p.ammo`) empties first, then each reload draws a round from `Armour.crewOf` stores: built-in first, then racks, then autoloader. Reload ×1.5 with no living loader; an autoloader gives a fixed time for guns ≥100 mm.
  - Shell select: `Aim.select` queues the next round; the same key twice within 1 s unloads and reloads now.
  - Automatic guns: held fire per substep with their own `p.cool` (the chosen gun on the trigger, the MGs on `F.mgFiring`), barrels spin, `p.gunOn` is set for other players' screens.
  - A main-gun shot: recoil through `v.applyImpulse(trunnion, −dir, 0.5·kg·v0)`, `p.shotAt`, flash/ring/smoke FX plus dust when the muzzle is under 3 m, `Sound.cannon`, `MP.sendShot`.
  - Launchers: stowed rounds refill the tubes after `reload` s standing still.
  - Also: `Aim.netFire` (other players' autocannons, for show), `Aim.solve`, `Aim.rangeTable`/`rocketEl`, `Aim.status` (one reused object per craft, §16.2 shape plus extras), `Aim.summary`.
- **Radars.**
  - Search radar: the antenna sweeps at its rpm; blips refresh at 2 Hz as the sweep passes them (at most 10). Aircraft are lost in clutter below 40 m over the ground and under 40 m/s along the beam.

  - `Aim.straight`: aimed missiles with nothing to steer for hold their heading.

deviations: Ballistic solve: the spec's ½g·t² with t(D) overstates the drop by about 9% at 2 km (several metres). I used the drag-exact small-angle drop instead, g·cosθ·(e^{2a}−1−2a)/(4(kρv)²) with a = kρR, taken across the line of sight (so climbing AA shots are right) with a small correction for speed lost climbing. Aim.solve takes an optional 5th argument, alt.

Ammunition model: p.ammo is the gun's ready rack (weapon.ammo). It empties first; after that every reload draws one round from Armour.crewOf().stores (built-in mods, then racks, then the autoloader). manned(v) needs a gunner or the commander. A design with no gunner role at all lets any living crew member except the driver fire; one whose gunner has died waits for 2B's role swap.

Aimed missiles with nothing to steer for (no lock, wire cut, lock lost) hold their heading (Aim.straight). The boost and the 0.05 s motor alone still let a level launch from a low launcher sag into the ground within about a second, which the 'no dive' test requires.

Top-attack missiles keep their target in s.tgt and leave s.target null. Otherwise moveShot's proximity fuse could burst them just above the roof (and they would show as homing on the target). The terminal dive aims at the target's top (its roof) rather than its centre of mass, so even a 20–30° dive comes in through the roof.
SACLOS and the command SAM add a lead term on the moving guidance point. Without it, a pure 'point 150/200 m ahead on the line' lags about 8 m on an 8 m/s crossing target at 2 km.

The traverse sweep tests box and disc footprints (with overlapping heights) against parts that don't turn and stand above the ring's top + 0.05. That keeps sweep(parts, group) pure without the adjacency map. yawLim may extend past ±180° one way, with the ring's yaw kept unwrapped inside it.
The sweep result also carries deps (each aimed part's {a: Float32Array(12), own}); group.dep is the main weapon's.
The rocket range table has 21 paths (5° to 55° in 2.5° steps) stepped at 1/120 s, with a fall angle per path. I added Aim.rocketEl(def, D, dH, body) for the inverse.

Combat.status for aimed guns: name like '85 mm APHE' (or 'MG'), ammo = every round aboard, plus reload (0..1) and ready. The smoke key is added only when smoke parts are aboard, so old craft get exactly the old object.

The ground radars' clutter rule is my own aimNotch (under 40 m over the ground and under 40 m/s along the beam, as §7.1 says), not Combat.clutter's 300 m rule. Radar line of sight uses aimClear, a copy of clearLine, which isn't exported.
Smoke replication: the cm message carries P = where the grenade set off and D = its velocity over a 0.8 s flight, so receivers grow the same cloud in the same place.
Aim assist moves Flight.aimYaw/aimPitch (3F's aim state) only when they are numbers; otherwise it does nothing. It reads Settings.get('aimAssist'), defaulting to on for touch.

findings.title: Tandem ATGMs (and old AGMs and rockets) skip the armour resolver when the first part they touch has no def.armour: one Reactive Bricks part, a smoke launcher or the gun barrel stops the jet completely
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Overbuilt/0587f056-6c41-58cd-9f76-3deee688a95a/scratchpad/ground/review-p2/armour/atgm-era.js — run: node atgm-era.js (also topattack-first.js for how often a top-down hit lands on an unarmoured part first)
findings.expected: The atgmTube (650 mm, tandem: 'Their tandem warheads go through reactive armour') fired by the real Aim.fire/launchMissile at a TK-34 turret face goes through it. With a brick on that face, the precursor sets the brick off (resolve's tandem rule) and the jet still kills the crew. Calling Armour.legacyHit directly on the brick does exactly that: gunner and commander dead.
findings.actual: Hook 30 is `if (hit.def.armour) return Armour.legacyHit(...)`. era (and smokeL, every gun, MG, sight, radar, launcher and seat) has no def.armour, so the missile takes the old path: a 3 m blast with he 3·blast = 9 mm. Bare turret: 'gunner DEAD, commander DEAD'. With a brick or a smoke launcher in front, nobody is hurt and the resolver is never called. From straight above, 22% of hits on an MA-1 meet an unarmoured part first (mostly gun120, mgHeavy, thermal).
findings.fix: Gate hook 30 on the vessel, not on the part: `if (hv.plated && hit.def.gv) return Armour.legacyHit(...)`, or at least `hit.def.armour || hit.def.era`. resolve already handles unarmoured parts: the jet carries on, and ERA and tandem follow their rules.

findings.title: Point blank: a muzzle pushed into an enemy turret (barrels aren't in the collision boxes) fires a shell that passes through the turret and its crew without a scratch
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Overbuilt/0587f056-6c41-58cd-9f76-3deee688a95a/scratchpad/ground/review-p2/armour/point-blank.js — run: node point-blank.js (the bare mechanism, a 120 mm dart started 0.3 m inside a turret: muzzle-inside.js)

The shooter lays on the target's turret face and fires through the real trigger. The 85 mm APHE round hits the turret armour it starts in (or treats it as entered at the muzzle) and penetrates.
findings.actual: The shooter's muzzle sits inside the target's turretCast. moveShell takes only hits with t0 >= 0, and resolve, cast from 5 cm back, skips the turret again (`if (h.t0 < -1e-6) continue`). Result: fired 1, Armour.fb.shot null, target not hurt, all 5 crew alive. The same dart fired from 10 m kills two of the turret crew.

Or start shells at the trunnion and test the barrel's own length as the first segment.

findings.title: Detonation throws the wrong turret: toss() throws v.tg[0], the lowest ring (first in part order on a tie), so an MG cupola ring on the hull deck flies off and the main turret stays on the hulk
findings.expected: Spec §6.6: on a detonation the turret (the outer group holding the main gun, or the one whose store went up) is cut from its base and thrown. Here the store that cooks off is in the main turret (turretCast).
findings.actual: Groups are [ringS:mgHeavy, ringM:turretCast+gun85]: equal tops, and the cupola was built first. The thrown piece is 'mgHeavy'. The hulk keeps 'hullMedium+trackMed+trackMed+engDiesel+ringS+ringM+turretCast+gun85'.
findings.fix: Throw the top-level ancestor of the group that holds the detonating store (det.st.part, or det.st.host through v.tgOf). With no such group (ammunition in the hull), throw the heaviest group without a parent (g.mass), not v.tg[0].

findings.title: Rocket artillery (HE rockets carrying s.he) gets the old rocket pods' 120 mm shaped charge on a direct hit, ×3 damage inside: one HE rocket knocks out a Tygr through 100 mm
findings.expected: Spec §7.6: MLRS rockets are HE, carry s.he, and the blast decides. A mlrsLight rocket (he 25, blast 10, dmg 600) bursting on a Tygr's 100 mm turret front can't get inside. Blast only: all five crew alive.
findings.actual: legacyHit sets `LG.type = 'heat'; LG.pen = s.pen || (s.k === 'rocket' ? 120 : ...)` for every k 'rocket', so the HE rocket penetrates 100 mm as a 120 mm HEAT jet doing 3 × 600 = 1,800 a module along its path. Real fireRocket → moveShot → legacyHit: the Tygr's ammunition detonates (ko 'ammo', turret thrown).
findings.fix: In legacyHit, send new HE rockets (s.he != null, or a fired part with def.aim) the way of bombs: `Combat.explode(…, s.he, spare); return false`. Keep the HEAT 120 row for old rocket pods only.

findings.title: Reactive bricks go off for machine-gun ball rounds: each 7.62 mm round that meets a brick tears it off
findings.expected: 'Explosive armour bricks: each one blows apart the first shaped charge or dart that hits it.' A coaxial MG's ball round should at most chip a brick (dmg 9 against its 40 hp), as old aircraft MGs do through the old path.
findings.actual: The resolver's ERA branch handles every non-burst round alike: `pen -= era.ke; add(R.rows, p, Combat.maxHp(D))`. Six ball8 rounds, one at each of six bricks on a TK-34's engine deck: 'brick torn off' six times, 0 of 6 left (each with a 'Reactive Bricks shot off!' toast, explosion sound and haptic buzz).
findings.fix: Set a brick off only with HEAT or a kinetic round above a calibre or penetration floor (for example cal >= 20 or pen >= 30). Below that, add the round's own dmg to the brick and stop the round.

findings.title: One HE shell on an ERA-covered tank tears off 18 parts one ripParts call at a time: about 32-36 ms of CPU (Node) and 20 toasts with 18 explosion sounds and buzzes
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Overbuilt/0587f056-6c41-58cd-9f76-3deee688a95a/scratchpad/ground/review-p2/armour/he-era-stall.js — run: node he-era-stall.js (cost breakdowns: pen-timing2.js, pen-timing3.js)
findings.expected: A hit costs a frame-sized amount (§14: a penetration and what follows ≤ 100 µs; no stutters). The player hears one blast and gets at most a toast or two.
findings.actual: The he120 shell on an MA-1 with 16 Reactive Bricks: explode damages each brick (no armour: all of k), and every brick destroyed goes separately through destroyPart → Flight.ripParts. Each call does a splitComponents and two rebuildGroups of a ~30-part tank, plus a toast, Sound.explode and haptic. Measured: 18 parts torn off, 31.8-35.6 ms for the one shell, 20 toasts ('Reactive Bricks shot off!' ×16, 'Side Skirt shot off!' ×2, 'Main gun destroyed', 'Coaxial MG destroyed').
